note:
DFlash2 draft-phase rules, read off the draft ranges of the 20260920_0 NSYS capture. One rule set, not a chain: every rule here is keyed on a kernel name that occurs exactly once per draft program position, or on a name plus an immediate program-order neighbour that disambiguates it, so no two rules can claim a position with different operations and the order they are tried in cannot change the result.

This file is deliberately partial. The draft decoder layer runs ~60 kernels, and roughly forty of them are bare `elementwise_kernel` / `vectorized_elementwise_kernel` launches belonging to the four grouped-convolution halves. Those cannot be separated by name and their neighbours are each other, so labeling them soundly needs the conv halves decomposed on the simulator side first -- which is the disposition this capture recommends, not something a rule can paper over. Until then they stay unmapped rather than being guessed into a slot.

The two `ncclDevKernel_AllGather_RING_LL` launches between the selector's two top-k selections are the other deliberate omission. They are the `get_top_k_tokens` value and id all-gathers, and the selector worklet does not price them, so mapping them would compare measured time against a slot that does not exist.

rules.name: nvjet_sm100_tst_256x192_64x4_2x1_2cta_v_bz_splitK_TNT
rules.role: projection of the six collected target hidden states down to the draft width
rules.note: This tile occurs once in the whole draft program, at its k=36864 shape. The splitK reduce that follows it is a second rule.

rules.name: cublasLt::splitKreduce_kernel
rules.role: projection of the six collected target hidden states down to the draft width
rules.note: splitKreduce runs after every split-K GEMM in the draft, so the predicate is the GEMM it reduces, never the name alone.

rules.name: nvjet_sm100_tst_64x128_64x13_2x1_2cta_v_bz_TNT

rules.role: norm of the projected hidden state before the fused KV projection
rules.note: The same rms_norm template also runs in the draft's input embedding; the input-prep kernel in front of this one is what separates them.

rules.name: vllm::rms_norm_kernel<c10::BFloat16, (int)8, (int)4, (bool)1>
rules.role: per-head K norm over tokens x layers x KV heads
rules.note: The (8, 4) template occurs once in the draft; the layer's q_norm and k_norm use a different one.

rules.name: vllm::rotary_embedding_kernel
rules.role: one rope call over tokens x layers
rules.note: The decoder layer runs the same kernel; the grouped K norm only precedes the context-KV one.

rules.name: vllm::rotary_embedding_kernel
rules.role: rope on the draft layer's own Q and K
rules.note: The fp8 query quantization only follows the layer's rope, never the context-KV one.

rules.name: cublasLt::splitKreduce_kernel
rules.role: fused gate and up projection

rules.name: trtllm_mnnvl_allreduce::oneshotAllreduceFusionKernel
rules.role: TP reduction of the draft attention output
rules.note: Both of the layer's collectives follow the same tile; they are separated in a second pass once the neighbouring operations carry labels.

rules.name: flashinfer::sampling::RadixTopKKernel_Unified
rules.role: radix select of this rank's top candidates out of its own vocabulary shard
rules.note: The vocabulary top-k is two selections, not one. `LogitsProcessor.get_top_k_tokens` never all-gathers the logits: each rank selects `top_k` from its own 38720-column shard, the ranks all-gather the values and the ids, and a second selection takes the global `top_k` out of the 64 gathered candidates. flashinfer's `top_k` dispatches on width, so the two calls land on different kernels and the capture separates them by name alone: the radix path here for the shard, the filtered path below for the gathered block. Both occur exactly once per draft program position in all 18 draft sequences.

rules.name: flashinfer::sampling::StableSortTopKByValueKernel
rules.role: on-device value sort of the shard selection's output
rules.note: `_topk` passes `sorted=True`, so each of the two selections ends in this sort; the same template instantiation runs for both, 36 launches against 18 draft sequences. Name alone cannot say which selection a launch belongs to, so each rule names the selection kernel immediately in front of it. The two predicates are disjoint and neither can fire on the other's position, so the order the rules are tried in does not matter. The simulator prices the sort inside the `logits_topk` leaf, because the profiled callable is the whole `flashinfer.top_k(..., sorted=True)` launch sequence rather than the select kernel alone.

rules.name: flashinfer::sampling::FilteredTopKUnifiedKernel
rules.role: filtered select of the global top candidates out of the all-gathered block
rules.note: The second `_topk`, over `top_k * tp_size` = 64 columns. flashinfer takes its filtered path at this width instead of the radix path, which is why no neighbour predicate is needed to tell the merge select from the shard select.

rules.name: flashinfer::sampling::FinalizeTopKIndicesKernel
rules.role: resolves the merge selection's column indices
rules.note: Second launch of the filtered path, so it belongs to the same merge selection as the kernel above. The radix path the shard select takes has no equivalent index pass.

rules.name: flashinfer::sampling::StableSortTopKByValueKernel
rules.role: on-device value sort of the merge selection's output
rules.note: The merge selection's half of the sorted=True pair; see the shard selection's sort rule for why the predicate is the preceding kernel.
